chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, from Abu Baseer, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him):
O you who believe! Turn to Allah with a sincere repentance
He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is the sin which is not repeated, ever!'
I said, 'Which of us do not repeat?'
So he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu Muhammad! Allah (exalted is He) Loves from His servant, the Tried one, the repentant'.
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of sincere repentance (Tawbah Nasuhah) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) offers a nuanced exegesis of 'tawbah nasuhah' (sincere repentance), defining it not as sinless perfection but as the consistent return to Allah after being tested. This aligns with the Shia scholarly emphasis on the 'muftan al-tawwab' (the tested and repentant servant), highlighting that divine love is often associated with those who struggle with worldly trials yet persist in repentance, rather than those who never err. The dialogue underscores the practical reality of human fallibility and the spiritual value of continuous self-correction.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, from Abu Baseer who said,

(What about) [66:8] O you who believe! Turn to Allah with a sincere repentance?’ Heasws said: ‘It is the sin which is not repeated, ever!’ I said, ‘Which of us do not repeat?’ So heasws said: ‘O Abu Muhammad! Allahazwj Loves from Hisazwj servant, the Tried one, the repentant’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from abu Ayyub from abu Basir who has said the following: “

Once I asked abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) about the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, ‘Believers, turn to Allah in repentance, “In a Nasuh manner,” with the intention of never repeating the same sin.’ [66:8]
The Imam said, ‘It is the sin that one never repeats.’
I then asked, ‘Who among us does not repeat?’
The Imam said, ‘O abu Muhammad, of His servants Allah loves those who are put to trial and the ones who repent very often.’”
